note: Labeled history blocks for the judge calibration harness (calibration_test.go). Each case is one atomic history block with the verdict a careful operator would give it, and the labels are the corpus's whole value: extend this file with blocks from real traces, keep the labels honest, and the two thresholds stop being guesses. Add a case rather than editing one when you disagree with a label, so the disagreement stays visible. Labels are keep (live state the agent is still working from), ledger (a decision, constraint, artifact or dead end worth keeping compressed) and prune (superseded output with no lasting value).
goal: Add ratio-based context compaction to bulle: a soft tier that tombstones old tool results, a mid tier that classifies each history block, and a state ledger the fold writes into. Package layout, the filet ceilings and the invariant list are fixed.

cases.text: assistant: The Judge interface returns one Verdict per block, in the order the blocks were given. A missing or short answer defaults to Keep, so a provider that answers about fewer blocks than it was asked can never cause a prune.

cases.label: ledger
cases.text: assistant: Invariant I1: every ToolResult in the outgoing conversation is preceded by the assistant message carrying the matching ToolCall. Prune removes whole atomic blocks only, which is what keeps that true.

cases.label: ledger
cases.text: assistant: The judge stays off by default. Enabling it sends conversation history — source code, possibly secrets — to a third party, so it is an explicit opt-in and never a shipped default.
